description: A single-panel figure rendered as a data table (no axes, curves, micrographs or scale bars) with a column-header row and five data rows, identified by the caption as "Table V. Effect of carbon on room-temperature tensile properties of hot-rolled AIM Fe-7Al alloy". The header reads, left to right, "Sl. no.", "Alloy composition (wt.%)", "Bulk hardness (HV)", then a spanning heading "Tensile properties (RT)" over three sub-columns "UTS (MPa)", "YS (MPa)" and "EL (%)". The rows list five hot-rolled Fe-7Al alloys with increasing carbon: Fe-7Al-.002C, Fe-7Al-0.15C, Fe-7Al-0.35C, Fe-7Al-0.5C and Fe-7Al-1.0C, each with a ± standard deviation on every value. Bulk hardness rises monotonically 193 ± 5.8 → 221 ± 6.9 → 248 ± 8.1 → 275 ± 9.2 → 338 ± 9.8 HV; UTS rises 425 ± 4.5 → 481 ± 5.2 → 515 ± 5.6 → 928 ± 6.8 → 1120 ± 8.2 MPa; YS rises 382 ± 6.3 → 452 ± 6.8 → 480 ± 7.2 → 652 ± 7.5 → 891 ± 9.2 MPa; elongation falls 21 ± 2.2 → 16 ± 1.8 → 13 ± 1.5 → (printed "08") ± 1.1 → 1.5 ± 0.5 %. The table demonstrates that carbon in Fe-7Al strongly raises hardness and strength while sharply lowering RT ductility, the largest strength jump occurring between Fe-7Al-0.35C and Fe-7Al-0.5C.

observations.observation: The header groups UTS (MPa), YS (MPa) and EL (%) under the single spanning heading "Tensile properties (RT)", with separate columns "Sl. no.", "Alloy composition (wt.%)" and "Bulk hardness (HV)".
Row 1, Fe-7Al-.002C: bulk hardness 193 ± 5.8 HV, UTS 425 ± 4.5 MPa, YS 382 ± 6.3 MPa, EL 21 ± 2.2 %.
Row 2, Fe-7Al-0.15C: bulk hardness 221 ± 6.9 HV, UTS 481 ± 5.2 MPa, YS 452 ± 6.8 MPa, EL 16 ± 1.8 %.
Row 3, Fe-7Al-0.35C: bulk hardness 248 ± 8.1 HV, UTS 515 ± 5.6 MPa, YS 480 ± 7.2 MPa, EL 13 ± 1.5 %.
Row 4, Fe-7Al-0.5C: bulk hardness 275 ± 9.2 HV, UTS 928 ± 6.8 MPa, YS 652 ± 7.5 MPa; the elongation cell is printed as "08 ± 1.1" (no % sign and leading zero), so the intended value is ambiguous.
Row 5, Fe-7Al-1.0C: bulk hardness 338 ± 9.8 HV, UTS 1120 ± 8.2 MPa, YS 891 ± 9.2 MPa, EL 1.5 ± 0.5 %.
Bulk hardness increases monotonically with carbon content across the five alloys, from 193 ± 5.8 HV (Fe-7Al-.002C) to 338 ± 9.8 HV (Fe-7Al-1.0C).
UTS and YS increase monotonically with carbon; the largest single step in both is between Fe-7Al-0.35C (UTS 515, YS 480 MPa) and Fe-7Al-0.5C (UTS 928, YS 652 MPa).
Elongation decreases monotonically with increasing carbon, from 21 ± 2.2 % at Fe-7Al-.002C to 1.5 ± 0.5 % at Fe-7Al-1.0C.
Every tabulated value is given with an accompanying ± standard deviation; no raw load-displacement or stress-strain curves are shown.

The caption states the figure is "Table V. Effect of carbon on room-temperature tensile properties of hot-rolled AIM Fe-7Al alloy"; the image itself shows only the column headers and does not print this title.

The caption states the alloys are hot-rolled and that the tensile properties were measured at room temperature (RT) and in the bulk hardness (HV) condition; these processing/test conditions are not printed in the image.
The figure demonstrates that increasing carbon in Fe-7Al raises room-temperature strength and hardness at the cost of ductility, i.e. a strength-ductility trade-off across the five compositions.
